Subject: MAP kickoff: VPC pilot, evaluation checkpoints, and commercial triggers

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. IndustrialAI is excited to evaluate Redwood in a private VPC for our pilot. Procurement asked me to put together an initial mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align milestones to procurement milestones (PO, legal signoff, invoice schedule). High level asks from my side:

- A 12-week pilot scope with three evaluation checkpoints (week 2 smoke test, week 6 perf/latency report, week 12 acceptance).
- Pricing anchors for pilot (monthly platform fee + committed GPU hours) and post-pilot ramp pricing tied to commit tiers.
- Clarity on private/VPC licensing: perpetual vs term license, platform fee mechanics, and SOC2 evidence.

Can you share a template MAP that maps milestones to economic triggers (discounts, commits, SLA inclusion) and a strawman for platform fee during pilot vs production? If we can get this into a shared doc today we’ll circulate to Procurement.

Thanks —
Emily

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: VPC pilot, evaluation checkpoints, and commercial triggers

Emily —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a working MAP and a draft SOW that ties acceptance gates to commercial events:
- Week 0: PO / signed SOW (triggers access provisioning).
- Week 2: Smoke acceptance (basic inference, latency within agreed envelope) — triggers 25% of pilot commit invoiced.
- Week 6: Performance report (throughput and cost-per-token baseline) — triggers review for optional burst capacity and 50% discount eligibility on platform fee for first quarter of production if baseline sustained.
- Week 12: Acceptance and handover — triggers final pilot invoice and option to convert to 12/24 month reserved capacity commit with tiered discounts.

Key commercial strawman (pilot):
- Pilot platform fee: $6,000/month (covers private control plane, monitoring, 5TB logging retention).
- Pilot compute commit: 800 GPU-hours (billed at committed rate; overage capped).
- If IndustrialAI signs for 24-month reserved capacity within 30 days of acceptance, Redwood offers a start-of-production discount grid: 10% at 2K hrs/mo commit, 18% at 4K hrs/mo, 28% at 8K hrs/mo.

We included an explicit platform fee credit: if production usage reaches 4K hrs/mo in the first quarter, Redwood will credit 50% of the platform fee for one month (applied to the first invoice after conversion).

Attached: IndustrialAI_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with dates/owners), SOW-draft-IndustrialAI-v1.pdf, SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Next steps: if Procurement needs adjusted invoice terms (net-45 vs net-30) or an alternative billing cadence, flag that now — we can adapt the MAP but pricing anchors should remain stable. Happy to schedule a 30-minute MAP walkthrough with you + procurement.

—Alex

Looping in a couple of internal comments on the draft MAP and pricing anchors:

- Platform fee: the pilot fee of $6k/mo is reasonable for the private control plane + support. For conversion, recommend making the platform fee a separate line item (not folded into commit) with a two-tier reduction tied to commit: 30% reduction at >=4K hrs, 55% reduction at >=8K hrs. That keeps our invoicing flexible.
- Commit vs ramp: suggest a staged commit: initial production commit of 2K hrs/mo for three months, then automatic ramp to 4K hrs/mo if both performance SLA and quality regressions are within thresholds. Put the automatic ramp as an opt-in clause to avoid surprise invoices.
- Discounts: we can compress discount steps to simplify negotiations: 10% (2K), 20% (4K), 35% (8K) — removes some negotiation noise and aligns with expected unit economics.
- Platform fee credit instead of one-time credit: offer a pro-rata platform fee waiver for the first 30 days post-conversion if commit >= 4K. Easier operationally.

I also recommend adding an acceptance criteria appendix in the MAP (SLOs + eval prompts) so Emily's engineers can run deterministic tests. I added commentary in tab 3 of the MAP spreadsheet.

Marissa
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
[internal note: confirm legal on auto-ramp clause before finalizing SOW]

Thanks — the MAP looks good overall. A few procurement asks before we proceed to signature: 

1) Can Redwood accept a net-45 payment term for the pilot invoices? IndustrialAI has standard net-45 for proof-of-concept work.
2) We need a clearer definition of the pilot acceptance (what constitutes pass/fail) and evidence required (logs, eval prompts, latency percentile numbers). Can you populate the acceptance appendix with exact metric thresholds?
3) Platform fee: procurement is pushing back on a recurring platform fee beyond the pilot without a clear commitment; they asked if we can structure the platform fee as a one-time setup fee during pilot and migrate to a reduced recurring platform fee only upon conversion.

If you can update the MAP per above, I’ll circulate to legal and procurement and aim for a PO by 8/27. We may also need an executive approval call the week of 8/24 to unblock budget signoff.

—Emily

Emily — thanks for the clear procurement asks. Quick alignment from our side and next steps: 

- Net terms: we can accommodate net-45 for the pilot only; production invoices will revert to net-30 (note included in MAP).
- Acceptance appendix: Marissa has added exact thresholds to the MAP (tab: Acceptance Criteria). Short summary: 95th pctl latency <= 220ms for small-batch inference, throughput within 10% of baseline profile, and no more than 0.5% quality regressions on the core eval set. Logs and KV cache artifacts required for the week-6 report.
- Platform fee mechanics: Redwood can structure the pilot as a one-time setup fee of $10k (covers private control plane and SOC2 evidence access), and then a reduced recurring platform fee of $3k/mo upon conversion (goes down per commit tier as described). We will capture the setup fee as a credit toward the first production invoice if customer converts within 60 days.
